geometry_intent.source: a broken crown forks around a real hanging root and an inward-facing hollow
geometry_intent.upper_outline: two separated thick boughs; no repeated platform column
geometry_intent.visual_acceptance: unverified; shared renderer is a consumer, not an art verdict

play_contract.alternative: Landing on the outer bark roof and finding its far edge early is a legitimate discovery; do not enforce a crown-visited counter.
play_contract.counterexample: Try an immediate entry walk-off toward the cache, a first-bough fall, zero-H ordinary jumps, missed second jump, and the right-root recovery.
play_contract.decision: Continue from the crown, descend around its back for the cache, or leave early through the lower root into a different world branch.
play_contract.new_information: After the outer fall, the hollow faces back toward the tree just crossed; its lower mouth later reveals the departure from below.
play_contract.observe: The crown's outer root hides the cache from an entry-side fall. Crossing above reveals the outside descent and an inward-facing opening.
play_contract.reward: Optional thorn crossing into an inward cache; reward and onward are different ports. The world owns the real OR transaction.
play_contract.world_requirement: Crown descends by main_to_far to return/back_return on the east side of the descending root and onward toward Boss. Failure and lower_return escape through the real western window to west_return, which the world must connect to an earlier root. Same support does not make the two sides mutually walkable.

geometry_intent.cache: the left hollow contains a voluntary floor-thorn crossing under a separately rooted thorn ceiling
geometry_intent.choice: the pocket allows a real outer drop; the inner direction reverses left across a gap, then right over a lower gap
geometry_intent.failure: a lower root catches the final gap; its outward low port must reconnect to the world
geometry_intent.outline: two rooted asymmetric bodies with an open middle, not three parallel shelves or a rectangular thorn frame
geometry_intent.source: a hollow western root bends under an outward bough, facing a thin living pocket on an eastern root
geometry_intent.visual_acceptance: unverified; the actual shared-renderer composition must be reviewed

play_contract.alternative: Ordinary held jumps remain legal; the actual rooted fruits also remain available to normal player input. This candidate declares no unconsumed hook choreography.
play_contract.counterexample: Try an immediate entry fall, a first-branch fall, direct pocket drop, no-H inward jump and a missed final jump; an early outer-bark approach is legal and must not receive a free cache.
play_contract.decision: Drop directly through the pocket for easier onward travel, or reverse left into the hollow and then right across the lower gap.
play_contract.failure: The final gap has a visible lower root and an explicit lower world escape. Recovery is incomplete until that actual port joins the world.
play_contract.new_behavior: The second direction reversal follows real stable reception; the Z is a route through open root bodies, not a command sequence password.
play_contract.observe: The thin eastern branch is a safe read point: the outer descent, inward fruit, left hollow and next lower root can be compared.
play_contract.reward: The left cache requires an additional outward-and-back thorn crossing. The world must execute a real richer OR reward; the factory awards nothing.
play_contract.world_requirement: Connect entry to its actual neighbour; after every local arrival at crown, execute crown_onward through the real eastern root window before the world continuation from onward. Connect failure_out to a real lower loop or separately verified recovery. Neither a full platform rectangle nor a local catch proves those world connections.
